newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks fall, but smaller issues gain.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks fall, but smaller issues gain.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Tuesday, but the broader market rose as investors sought undervalued technology shares and smaller issues.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 11.55 points to 6,510.15.
In the broader market, however, advancing issues outnumbered decliners by nearly two-to-one on the New York Stock Exchange on heavy volume of more than 285 million shares.
The technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index jumped 11.73 to 1,311.55, surpassing Monday's record, which was its sixth consecutive closing high.
Technology stocks dominated both the NYSE and Nasdaq leader boards.
"The market had been boosted by a scenario that said the economy was cooling and rates were coming down," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.

"What we're seeing now is that people's outlook on the economy has improved somewhat," he said. "That may be at odds with the bond market but it has allowed people to move back into growth fields like technology."
The trickling down of the rally was viewed as a positive by analysts, some of whom had watched with concern as blue chips stage an essentially one-pronged advance.
"Market internals are extremely strong today," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "There's an undeniable broadening of the market."
Bleier cautioned, "some Nasdaq and small-cap names are moving up big percentages quickly and that is a sign you have a bit of speculation taking place in tech stocks."
Stocks also benefitted from an increasingly favourable interest rate environment, as bond prices continued to push higher after news of a sharp drop in new home sales and a firming dollar.
The Commerce Department reported seasonally adjusted sales of new single-family homes fell by 8.7 percent in October, a much sharper decline than economists had forecast.

The data confirmed a softening trend in the housing market and helped bonds to add to early gains. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose a quarter point to yield 6.34 percent, down from 6.36 percent at Monday's close.
The dollar rose to 1.5628 German marks from 1.5545 marks late Monday, but fell to 112.95 Japanese yen from 114.55 yen.
Among individual issues, Silicon Graphics Inc. jumped 3-1/4 to 23-1/2 after Goldman Sachs added the shares to its recommended list.

Among other NYSE listed technology issues posting solid gains were, America Online Inc., up 2-5/8 at 42-3/4, International Business Machines Corp., up 2-3/8 at 165-5/8, and Compaq Computer Corp., up 1-3/8 at 81-3/4.

Hutchinson Technology Inc. surged 17 to 69-3/4 after the company said it expected its fiscal first quarter earnings per share would be sharply higher than a year ago and would come in at more than double analysts' estimates.
